decisions.claim: B declined the invitation to join A and others at the concert this evening
decisions.reason: A's 'Why not?' in turn 3 strongly presupposes that B gave a negative response to the invitation in turn 1. This is a well-grounded inference from the presupposition structure of 'Why not?' — it is only natural to ask 'Why not?' when someone has said no or expressed unwillingness.
decisions.counterexample: B could have said something ambiguous that A interpreted as a refusal, but this is unlikely given the directness of 'Why not?' as a follow-up to a yes/no question.

decisions.claim: B declined or expressed unwillingness to join the concert this evening
decisions.reason: c2 makes the same core claim as c1 — that B expressed unwillingness/declined to join the concert. The slight broadening to 'declined or expressed unwillingness' does not add distinct information at this granularity; both capture the same presuppositional inference from 'Why not?'

design: dual route, targeted rescue, globally grouped evidence adjudication
